svg.title: A-430 Axonometric — Three Balcony Options
svg.text: LEVEL from the south-west · 1:250 @ A1 · METRES
Masonry wall cut by section — 200 mm
Internal stud or block partition, 120 mm
Single leaf door, swing shown to opening side
Glazed opening — arched head where noted
Element above the cut plane (pergola, slab
1. Preliminary. Isometric from the south-west, which is the
one corner that shows the street frontage, the blind west
wall, the roof pergola and the entrance garden at once.
2. This is a projection, not a render: every line is a
transform of the constants the plans are drawn from, so it
cannot show a balcony, a garden or a neighbour that the
3. All three sit on the real plot. The villa is hard against
the east boundary with a 1.00 m side passage and the 11.50
m entrance garden on the west, the three-storey blind
neighbour standing back behind it and the single-storey
clay-brick one a metre to the east.
4. A and C wear the same skin, so the only difference between
them is the curve — which is why they stand side by side
here. B differs in ornament as well.
5. The balconies stop at the corner on all three: the 1.00 m
setbacks forbid anything projecting west, north or east.
6. Faces are painted back to front rather than depth-sorted,
so a detail may overlap where two surfaces nearly touch.
The measured elevations A-400 to A-421 govern.
Preliminary design issue — not for construction.
Do not scale; work to figured dimensions only.
P13 2026-10-07 site plan redrawn for the detached villa
P14 2026-10-07 section A-A recut through the east strip, and marked on every plan
P15 2026-10-07 exterior: two schemes, elevations and balcony curves
P16 2026-10-07 neighbours as surveyed: west 3 storeys and blind, east single storey
